info.title: Field Shift API
info.description:
Contract between the frontend and backend of the Field Shift farmer map
(NASA Space Apps, crop-rotation decision support). THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH.
Change it first (PR + entry in CONTRACT_CHANGELOG.md), then change code.

## Conventions (apply everywhere)
- Base path `/v1`. JSON, UTF-8. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC (`2026-11-14T12:00:00Z`). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Coordinates in our own objects are `{ "lat": number, "lon": number }` (WGS84). NEVER bare arrays.
  The only exception is GeoJSON and bbox, which follow the GeoJSON spec: `[lon, lat]` and `[west, south, east, north]`.
- All numeric values are SI (m, mm, degC, m3/m3, g/kg, ha). The frontend converts to US units for display.
- A metric that cannot be provided is returned with `value: null` and `quality: unavailable` plus a reason. Never omit it and never invent it.
- Every metric states its `source` and `resolution_m`, because satellite data is often much coarser than a field.
- Errors always use the `ErrorResponse` envelope. Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header.
- Coverage v1: contiguous US (CONUS). Selectable land units exist only inside the regions listed by `GET /meta/coverage`.
- NAMING NOTE (v0.2): in API names, "field" means the *selectable land unit*. In v0.2 that unit is a
  **PLSS survey section** (BLM Public Land Survey System, about 1 square mile / 640 acres), NOT a farm field.
  Names like `field_id`, `/fields`, `FieldSelection` are kept to avoid breaking clients; the UI must say "survey section".
  The PLSS exists only in the surveyed states; elsewhere the backend falls back to a buffered point.
- Units are NEVER sent as bulk GeoJSON. They are drawn from vector tiles; see `/tiles/fields/...`.

get.summary: Where the app works and where field polygons are available
get.description: Frontend uses this to set map bounds, tile zoom thresholds and to warn users outside field coverage.

get.summary: One county (use its bbox to fit the map after the user picks it)

post.summary: Turn pasted text into a field selection (entry methods 2 and 3)
post.description:
The user pastes ONE string into one input. Backend detects the kind:
plain coordinates (`41.5868, -93.625`, also `41.5868 -93.625` and degrees/minutes/seconds),
a Google Maps URL (full or short link), or an Apple Maps URL (full or short link).
Short links are followed server-side (host allow-list, no other redirects).
The point is then resolved to a field (see `POST /fields/resolve`).

422.description:
Error codes: `UNPARSEABLE_INPUT` (not coordinates or a known link),
`UNSUPPORTED_LINK` (recognised link but no coordinates inside, typical for some Apple short links),
`OUTSIDE_COVERAGE` (valid point outside CONUS).

post.summary: Resolve a point (map click, coordinates) to a field selection
post.description:
Snaps to the nearest field polygon within `snap_radius_m`. If none is found, falls back to a buffered point
(`resolved_by = buffered_point`) so the user can still run an analysis.

get.summary: Get a field by id (landing-page click on a field tile)

get.description:
Mapbox Vector Tile. Layers: `states` (props: `fips`, `name`, `postal`), `counties` (props: `fips`, `name`, `state_fips`),
`townships` (props: `township_id`, `label`; PLSS townships, about 6 x 6 miles, only where PLSS data exists).
Suggested use: `states` at zoom < 7, `counties` at zoom 7 to 10, `townships` additionally at zoom 9 to 10,
then the `fields` tiles (sections) from `coverage.field_tiles.min_zoom`.

get.summary: Selectable land units (vector tile; PLSS sections in v0.2)
get.description:
Mapbox Vector Tile. Layer `fields`, props: `field_id` (string), `crop_class` (string, EMPTY in v0.2 because
PLSS has no crop data), `area_ha` (number), `label` (string, e.g. "Section 14, T8N R2E").
In v0.2 each feature is one PLSS section. Only served for z >= `coverage.field_tiles.min_zoom` inside covered regions;
elsewhere returns 204. The same data may be served as a static PMTiles file; the frontend must read
the tile URL template from `GET /meta/coverage` (`field_tiles.url_template`), not hardcode it.

post.summary: Base data for a selected field (fast, cached)
post.description:
Called as soon as a field is selected (landing click, or any of the 3 entry methods).
Target latency under 2 s; the backend caches by field_id or rounded point. Synchronous.
Metrics are the same shape the analysis uses, so the UI can reuse one component.

Triggered by "Get analysis". Returns 202 immediately with a job. Poll `GET /analyses/{job_id}`
every 2 s (back off to 5 s after 30 s). Identical requests within the cache window may return an existing job.

get.summary: Job status and, when finished, the result

200.description:
Job state. `result` is present only when `status = succeeded`; `error` only when `status = failed`.
A failed JOB still returns HTTP 200; HTTP errors are for failed REQUESTS.

BBox.description: [west, south, east, north] in degrees, GeoJSON order.

coordinates.description: Linear rings, each a list of [lon, lat]. First ring is the exterior.

FieldId.description:
Stable id of a selectable land unit. Opaque to the frontend. In v0.2 backend builds it from the BLM
section identifiers (`plss:` + First Division id, plus the duplicate suffix if the source has one),
so it only changes when the data version changes (see `Coverage.field_data_version`).

has_field_coverage.description: False means there are no selectable units (PLSS sections) in this county; the UI should offer point-based analysis instead.

unit.description: What the features in the `fields` tiles are. `plss_section` in v0.2.

url_template.description: XYZ template, e.g. `/v1/tiles/fields/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt` or a PMTiles URL.

regions.description: Areas where units exist (in v0.2, the states/areas that have PLSS data).

SelectionSource.description: How the user got here. Used for analytics and UI hints only; never changes results.

SelectionRef.description:
What the client sends to identify "the field". Give a `field_id` when you have one (preferred),
otherwise a `point`. Backend resolves it and returns the full `FieldSelection`.

FieldSelection.description: Backend-resolved selection. This is the one object every page works with.

anchor.description: Point used to sample point datasets (polygon centroid, or the clicked point).

geometry.description: The field polygon, or the buffered circle (approximated as a polygon) around the point.

resolved_by.description:
`field_polygon`: id lookup or point inside a polygon.
`snapped_point`: point snapped to nearest polygon within the snap radius.
`buffered_point`: no polygon nearby, a circle of `buffer_m` is used.

boundary_type.description:
`plss_section`: a BLM PLSS survey section (about 1 sq mile). It is a survey grid cell, NOT the
farmer's field and not an ownership boundary; a real field may be a part of it or span several.
The UI must say "survey section" and tell the user their field lies somewhere inside it.
`estimated_csb`: reserved for a later USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries layer (not served in v0.2).
`buffered_point`: no unit here (outside the PLSS area), a circle around the point is used.
Enum is extensible.

plss.description: PLSS identifiers. Present when `boundary_type = plss_section`, otherwise null.

label.description: Human-readable name of the unit for the UI (e.g. "Section 14, T8N R2E"); null for buffered points.

crop_class.description: Latest mapped crop, if known. Always null in v0.2 (PLSS has no crop data).

crop_history.description: Mapped crop per year, newest first. Always empty in v0.2; never guessed.

PlssRef.description: BLM PLSS identifiers (CadNSDI). Field names mirror BLM attributes.

point.description: The point as parsed from the input, before snapping.

key.description:
Stable machine key. Known keys (new ones may be added, the frontend must render unknown keys generically):
`soil_moisture_surface` (SMAP), `soil_moisture_rootzone` (SMAP L4), `relative_humidity_2m` (NASA POWER),
`air_temp_mean_2m`, `precip_30d_total`, `precip_annual_normal`, `soil_organic_matter_pct`,
`soil_nitrogen_total` (estimated), `soil_ph`, `soil_texture_class`, `elevation_m`, `slope_pct`.
`soil_wetness_surface` and `soil_wetness_rootzone` (NASA POWER, modeled, unit `fraction`).

value.description: Number for continuous metrics, string for classes (e.g. texture), null if unavailable.

unit.description: Machine unit: `m3/m3`, `%`, `degC`, `mm`, `g/kg`, `m`, `pH`, `class`, `fraction` (0 to 1, e.g. NASA POWER modeled soil wetness), `none`.

period.description: Averaging window for the value, if it is an aggregate.

quality.description: `estimated` = derived proxy (e.g. nitrogen from organic matter). UI must label it as an estimate.

resolution_m.description: Native spatial resolution in metres. Coarse values (greater than the field size) are shown with a warning.

crop_history.description: Optional. Newest first. In v0.2 there is no mapped crop data, so this is the only source of crop history; the UI should let the farmer enter it.

stage.description: Human-readable current step, safe to show to the user.

current_conditions.description: Same metric shape as the snapshot, possibly with more metrics.

time_series.description: Optional history for charts (e.g. soil moisture, precipitation).

strategies.description: At least 3 rotation strategies, one of which has `is_current = true`. Sorted by `score` descending.

disclaimer.description: Shown verbatim on the results page. The tool supports, not replaces, local expertise.

name.example: Corn / soybean with winter rye cover

is_current.description: True for the baseline (the farmer's existing rotation).

rotation.description: Ordered seasons of one rotation cycle.

score.description: Fit to this field and the chosen priorities. Comparable only inside this result.

summary.description: One or two plain-language sentences for a farmer.

evidence.description: Why it was suggested, tied to data.

needs_local_review.description: True when local agronomist or extension review is specifically advised.

message.description: Safe to show to the user.
